reasoning_traces.think:
The core operation involves constructing a multivariate regression framework where expert predictions serve as features and actual fantasy points as targets. The process begins with scraping expert rankings from 2015, treating these as input variables X ∈ ℝ^n×m, where n represents weeks and m denotes expert count. Actual points Y ∈ ℝ^n are collected as labels. Supervised learning algorithms from scikit-learn map this structure to predictive functions f(X) → Y. Each model M ∈ M is evaluated using RMSE or similar metrics to determine superiority. This approach leverages ensemble theory to reduce variance in predictions while maintaining bias control. Dualities emerge between expert consensus and statistical fit—when experts agree strongly, regression models should reflect high confidence. Failure modes include overfitting when too many features are used without regularization, or underfitting if the model is too simplistic. Temporal consistency must also be ensured across seasons to maintain validity.
